a 303 redirect, urllib3 switches the method to `GET` and drops the request body per RFC 9110, Section 15.4.4 — but the state that *describes* that body survives the switch. Two things go wrong as a result.

### 1. The redirected GET announces a body it never sends

With `chunked=True` (or an explicit `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header), the follow-up request goes out as:

```
GET /done HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
Accept-Encoding: identity
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
User-Agent: python-urllib3/2.x

0
```

A bodyless `GET` framed with chunked transfer encoding. Harmless against tolerant servers, but it is invalid framing for a request with no content, and strict servers and intermediaries reject it.

### 2. A file-like body makes the redirect fail outright

`body_pos` also survives the body being set to `None`, so urllib3 then tries to rewind a body that no longer exists:

```python
import urllib3

pool = urllib3.HTTPConnectionPool(host, port)
pool.urlopen("POST", "/", body=open("payload.bin", "rb"), redirect=True)
```

against a server answering `303 See Other`:

```
  File "urllib3/connectionpool.py", line 768, in urlopen
    body_pos = set_file_position(body, body_pos)
  File "urllib3/util/request.py", line 184, in set_file_position
    rewind_body(body, pos)
  File "urllib3/util/request.py", line 221, in rewind_body
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: body_pos must be of type integer, instead it was <class 'int'>.
```

The message is self-contradictory because it reports the type of `body_pos` while the actual failure is that `body` is `None` and has no `seek()`.

Both problems affect `HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen()` and `PoolManager.urlopen()`, so the top-level `urllib3.request()` is affected too.

## The fix

Following a 303 redirect, urllib3 switches the method to `GET` and drops the request body per RFC 9110, Section 15.4.4 — but the state that *describes* that body survives the switch. Two things go wrong as a result.

### 1. The redirected GET announces a body it never sends

With `chunked=True` (or an explicit `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header), the follow-up request goes out as:

```
GET /done HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
Accept-Encoding: identity
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
User-Agent: python-urllib3/2.x

0
```

A bodyless `GET` framed with chunked transfer encoding. Harmless against tolerant servers, but it is invalid framing for a request with no content, and strict servers and intermediaries reject it.

### 2. A file-like body makes the redirect fail outright

`body_pos` also survives the body being set to `None`, so urllib3 then tries to rewind a body that no longer exists:

```python
import urllib3

pool = urllib3.HTTPConnectionPool(host, port)
pool.urlopen("POST", "/", body=open("payload.bin", "rb"), redirect=True)
```

against a server answering `303 See Other`:

```
  File "urllib3/connectionpool.py", line 768, in urlopen
    body_pos = set_file_position(body, body_pos)
  File "urllib3/util/request.py", line 184, in set_file_position
    rewind_body(body, pos)
  File "urllib3/util/request.py", line 221, in rewind_body
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: body_pos must be of type integer, instead it was <class 'int'>.
```

The message is self-contradictory because it reports the type of `body_pos` while the actual failure is that `body` is `None` and has no `seek()`.

Both problems affect `HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen()` and `PoolManager.urlopen()`, so the top-level `urllib3.request()` is affected too.

## The fix

When the body is dropped, the state describing it goes with it:

- `HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen()` and `PoolManager.urlopen()`: reset `chunked = False` and `body_pos = None` in the 303 branch, alongsid

One change worth calling out, since it isn't obviously part of the fix:

`test_redirect_with_failed_tell` requested `/redirect`, whose default status is `303 See Other`, and asserted `UnrewindableBodyError`. With this fix the body is dropped on a 303 and so never needs rewinding, which makes that assertion no longer meaningful. I pointed the test at `status=307` so it keeps covering the rewind path (matching `test_redirect_put_file` in the same class), and added `test_303_redirect_with_failed_tell` for the 303 case.

Happy to split that into its own commit if you'd prefer it separated from the fix.

The one red check, `Ubuntu 3.13`, looks unrelated: `test_buffer_memory_usage_no_decoding[False-10485760-read]` allocated 11.0MiB against the `limit_memory("10.5 MB")` mark while reading 10MiB, so the margin is about five percent. Nothing in this branch touches response buffering, and the same job passed on the previous two pushes. A re-run should clear it whenever you get a chance.

While chasing an unrelated hang I also noticed `test_tunnel_sets_http_11_alpn` is flaky: it asserts `b"h2" not in self.buf` against the whole ClientHello, so it trips whenever those two bytes land in the random material, which is likelier now that the key share carries a post-quantum group. It failed twice in 300 local runs and once on Windows here. Glad to send a separate PR narrowing that assertion to the ALPN extension if that would be useful.

Regarding the hangs, would it make sense to add `await request.get_data()` at the beginning of dummyserver's `redirect` handler, and possibly to other dummyserver handlers as well in a separate PR?

> While chasing an unrelated hang I also noticed `test_tunnel_sets_http_11_alpn` is flaky: it asserts `b"h2" not in self.buf` against the whole ClientHello, so it trips whenever those two bytes land in the random material, which is likelier now that the key share carries a post-quantum group. It failed twice in 300 local runs and once on Windows here. Glad to send a separate PR narrowing that assertion to the ALPN extension if that would be useful.

A fix will be very welcome!

Done, that works well. `/redirect` now reads the body up front, with `parse_form_data=True` so `request.values` on the next line still sees form fields (same pattern as the `/upload` handler). The two framing tests no longer need to disguise their bodies as forms, so the workaround and the comment explaining it are gone.

Nice side effect: with the body drained, those tests now fail fast instead of hanging when the fix is absent, which makes them a lot friendlier to bisect against.

Verified locally: the framing tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix, 200 consecutive runs with no hang, and the rest of `test/with_dummyserver/` is unchanged either way.

### 1. The redirected GET announces a body it never sends

With `chunked=True` (or an explicit `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header), the follow-up request goes out as:

```
GET /done HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
Accept-Encoding: identity
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
User-Agent: python-urllib3/2.x

0
```

A bodyless `GET` framed with chunked transfer encoding. Harmless against tolerant servers, but it is invalid framing for a request with no content, and strict servers and intermediaries reject it.

### 2. A file-like body makes the redirect fail outright

`body_pos` also survives the body being set to `None`, so urllib3 then tries to rewind a body that no longer exists:

```python

pool = urllib3.HTTPConnectionPool(host, port)
pool.urlopen("POST", "/", body=open("payload.bin", "rb"), redirect=True)
```

ValueError: body_pos must be of type integer, instead it was <class 'int'>.

Following a 303 redirect, urllib3 switches the method to `GET` and drops the request body per RFC 9110, Section 15.4.4 — but the state that *describes* that body survives the switch. Two things go wrong as a result.

### 1. The redirected GET announces a body it never sends

With `chunked=True` (or an explicit `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` header), the follow-up request goes out as:

```
GET /done HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
Accept-Encoding: identity
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
User-Agent: python-urllib3/2.x

0
```

A bodyless `GET` framed with chunked transfer encoding. Harmless against tolerant servers, but it is invalid framing for a request with no content, and strict servers and intermediaries reject it.

### 2. A file-like body makes the redirect fail outright

`body_pos` also survives the body being set to `None`, so urllib3 then tries to rewind a body that no longer exists:

```python
import urllib3

pool = urllib3.HTTPConnectionPool(host, port)
pool.urlopen("POST", "/", body=open("payload.bin", "rb"), redirect=True)
```

against a server answering `303 See Other`:

```
  File "urllib3/connectionpool.py", line 768, in urlopen
    body_pos = set_file_position(body, body_pos)
  File "urllib3/util/request.py", line 184, in set_file_position
    rewind_body(body, pos)
  File "urllib3/util/request.py", line 221, in rewind_body
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: body_pos must be of type integer, instead it was <class 'int'>.
```

The message is self-contradictory because it reports the type of `body_pos` while the actual failure is that `body` is `None` and has no `seek()`.

Both problems affect `HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen()` and `PoolManager.urlopen()`, so the top-level `urllib3.request()` is affected too.

## The fix

When the body is dropped, the state describing it goes with it:

- `HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen()` and `PoolManager.urlopen()`: reset `chunked = False` and `body_pos = None` in the 303 branch, alongsid

One change worth calling out, since it isn't obviously part of the fix:

`test_redirect_with_failed_tell` requested `/redirect`, whose default status is `303 See Other`, and asserted `UnrewindableBodyError`. With this fix the body is dropped on a 303 and so never needs rewinding, which makes that assertion no longer meaningful. I pointed the test at `status=307` so it keeps covering the rewind path (matching `test_redirect_put_file` in the same class), and added `test_303_redirect_with_failed_tell` for the 303 case.

Happy to split that into its own commit if you'd prefer it separated from the fix.

The one red check, `Ubuntu 3.13`, looks unrelated: `test_buffer_memory_usage_no_decoding[False-10485760-read]` allocated 11.0MiB against the `limit_memory("10.5 MB")` mark while reading 10MiB, so the margin is about five percent. Nothing in this branch touches response buffering, and the same job passed on the previous two pushes. A re-run should clear it whenever you get a chance.

It failed twice in 300 local runs and once on Windows here. Glad to send a separate PR narrowing that assertion to the ALPN extension if that would be useful.
